title: Lazarus and the billion-dollar bank campaign

scenes.narration: [serious] America called them the world's top bank robbers. They never entered a bank.
From 2015 to 2019, officials say, a North Korean team hit banks in many countries.
Their plan was simple. First, break into a bank's computers. Then send fake orders to move money.
In total, they tried to take over 1.2 billion dollars.
Then they tried a new trick: cash machines. In 2018, a bank in Pakistan lost 6.1 million dollars.
Someone had to clean the stolen money. A man in Canada later admitted helping.
In 2021, three North Korean army hackers were charged. They robbed banks without walking inside.

facts.claim: Assistant Attorney General John Demers called North Korea's operatives 'the world's leading bank robbers'

From 2015 to 2019 the hackers allegedly attempted to steal more than $1.2 billion from banks in Vietnam, Bangladesh, Taiwan, Mexico, Malta and Africa by breaching networks and sending fraudulent SWIFT messages
In October 2018 $6.1 million was stolen from BankIslami Pakistan Limited in an ATM cash-out scheme
Ghaleb Alaumary, a Canadian-American of Mississauga, Ontario, agreed to plead guilty to laundering funds from the BankIslami and Indian ATM cash-outs and the February 2019 Maltese bank heist

Jon Chang Hyok, Kim Il and Park Jin Hyok, alleged members of North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau (Lazarus Group/APT38), were indicted; unsealed February 17, 2021; alleged scheme of more than $1.3 billion
Park Jin Hyok was first charged in a complaint filed June 8, 2018, which said the group attacked several other banks from 2015 to 2018
